newsitem.title: COMOROS: Secessionist protest on Comoros island.
newsitem.headline: Secessionist protest on Comoros island.

text.p: Secessionist protests erupted on the Indian Ocean Comoros island of Moheli on Wednesday with demonstrators burning tyres and setting up roadblocks, witnesses said.
The protesters said they were acting in support of secessionists on Anjouan island, where three people were killed in clashes with security forces on July 14.
"The struggle of the Anjouan people against injustice and humiliation is ours. We want to get out of the Comorian federation," said a statement by a group called the Moheli People Organisation.

The Comoro Islands, with a population of 190,000, became independent from France in 1975. Residents of Anjouan, the second island, argue independence has brought only poverty, civil strife and numerous coups.
Three people including a gendarme were killed on Anjouan on July 14 in clashes involving secessionists who tried to raise French flags on Bastille Day. Several people were killed in March.
The Moheli protests started on Tuesday afternoon when residents set up roadblocks from burning tyres and hoisted French national flags.
France has denounced the secessionists. It said the Anjouan situation was serious and could destabilise the whole region.
It is the third time protesters on Moheli, the smallest of four main islands in the Comoro federation, have demanded secession.
